design:
D1 — State only. The check asks three recorded questions: was the turn given a document (the delivered InboundQueueEntry.spec_document), was anything written into it (more than one `content` SpecDocumentEvent), and did this run create a Question. It never reads the agent's output; that is the capability's defining constraint.

D2 — Documents only; tasks belong to divergence. The check runs from evaluate_run_end only on the `not run.task_id` branch. A bound run, including a review, that produced nothing is a divergence, the stronger and actionable record.

D3 — A note, not a policy. The event is a warning for the operator; it starts no retry, parks nothing and returns no divergence id.

D4 — Visible outcome from run facts. A turn's closing label is derived from the run's recorded terminal status, so a reload shows the same; a completed turn gets its duration and no label. The client refetches run facts on a terminal run event and on stream reconnect rather than waiting for new content.

problem: A turn that failed, or that ended with its questions written as ordinary reply text, can look like any other: no label, no question row, an empty document. Without outcomes drawn from recorded facts, the operator only finds out by reading the transcript.

requirements.rationale: An agent that writes its questions as chat text and ends its turn leaves no question row and an empty document; the operator needs a visible record that the turn produced nothing. Exit status is not a condition, so a crashed run reads differently from a completed one only through the recorded status.
requirements.statement: When a run that is not bound to a task ends, and the input delivered in it named a specification document into which nothing has been written beyond its creation scaffold, and the run recorded no question, the Hub SHALL record a `turn_produced_nothing` warning event naming the run, the agent, the document, its phase and the run's exit status.

requirements.rationale: Guessing whether trailing prose is a question is a judgement the product does not make on the operator's behalf; the retired prose detector (dropped in migration 0082) must not return under another name.
requirements.statement: The determination SHALL use only recorded state — the delivered input's document, the document's write events and the run's question rows — and SHALL NOT read or interpret the agent's output text.

requirements.rationale: Both document-creation paths save a scaffold immediately, so creation-time fields are always populated and would make the check unreachable.
requirements.statement: A document SHALL count as written only when it has more than one `content` event; the scaffold write made at creation and any field populated at creation time (such as `content_digest`) SHALL NOT count as the document having advanced.

requirements.rationale: Most turns are conversation, and recording every chat reply would be noise; a bound run is already covered by run divergence, and returned input is about to be handled by another run, so nothing was dropped.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL NOT evaluate a run for this outcome when its delivered input named no specification document, when the run is bound to a task, or when the run's delivered input was returned to the queue for redelivery.

requirements.rationale: An operator reading a timeline must be able to tell a document nobody changed from a task nobody moved without opening either row.
requirements.statement: The operator's activity views SHALL summarise a `turn_produced_nothing` event as "<agent> ended (<exit status>) without changing <document>", worded differently from a run-divergence row.

requirements.rationale: An unsuccessful turn that ends silently reads as success; a success label on every turn is noise.
requirements.statement: The conversation SHALL label every turn whose run ended failed, stopped or interrupted with that outcome, SHALL present a completed turn with its duration and no closing label, and SHALL present the same after a page reload, from the run's recorded facts alone.

requirements.rationale: A run that ends with no further output, or while the client is disconnected, must still show how it ended.
requirements.statement: A client displaying a conversation SHALL refresh its run facts when a run for that agent reaches a terminal status (`run_completed`, `run_failed`, `run_stopped`, `run_interrupted`) and when its event stream reconnects, not only when new conversation content arrives.

in_scope: The terminal outcome label of each turn in the conversation, and refreshing it when a run ends or the stream reconnects
Runs not bound to a task whose delivered input named a specification document
The `turn_produced_nothing` event and its summary in the operator's activity views
non_goals: Runs bound to a task: a bound run that ends without moving its task is a run divergence (run-task-binding)
The exit-condition line in a specification turn's canonical context (agent-context-onboarding)
Normalising and rendering stream events within a turn (agent-stream-events)
Inferring from an agent's final message whether it asked something

summary: How the operator sees how a turn ended. The conversation labels every failed, stopped or interrupted turn from the run's recorded facts and refreshes when a run ends; and the Hub records an authoring turn that was given a specification document, wrote nothing into it and asked nothing, deciding from recorded state alone, never from the agent's prose.
